candidates.source_title: Hopwood Hall marks construction milestone for Clegg Building in Rochdale
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A topping out ceremony has marked a stage in the construction of Hopwood Hall College’s Clegg Building in Rochdale. The development, being built by Willmott Dixon, is funded by the Department for Education, Rochdale Council and the college and is scheduled to open in late 2027. The building is named after Robert Clegg OBE, who served as chair of the college’s corporation from 2007 to 2018 and died in September 2021. His wife Anne, son Richard and daughter Emma attended the ceremony. Emma is continuing the family’s connection with Hopwood Hall as a part-time adult learner. They joined principal and chief executive Julia Heap OBE, Rochdale MP Paul Waugh, and the Mayor and Mayoress of Rochdale, Faisal Rana and Iram Faisal, among other guests. Willmott Dixon staff led visitors to the roof, which overlooks landmarks including Rochdale Town Hall and St Chad’s Parish Church. Guests were invited to leave messages on part of the roof parapet as a permanent record of the occasion. The college says the building will provide technical learning facilities for students of all ages. School leavers attending its open events have also been given a glimpse of the development.

candidates.source_title: Springhill Hospice receives £1,500 donation towards running costs
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Springhill Hospice has received £1,500 from David Wilson Homes to help meet its general running costs. The donation was made through the Barratt Redrow Foundation, the housebuilding group’s charitable arm. The hospice has provided specialist palliative care since 1989, serving adults and their families across Rochdale, Middleton and Heywood. Its purpose-built facility has 16 beds and provides physical, psychological, emotional and spiritual care without charge. Vicki Barnett, senior corporate fundraiser at Springhill Hospice, said “This vital funding comes at a crucial time as the Hospice continues to navigate rising costs and increasing demand for palliative and end of life care services.” She added “Every donation we receive makes a genuine difference to the families we support, and we are deeply grateful for this generosity. It helps us continue providing compassionate care at the most difficult moments in people’s lives, and knowing our community stands behind us means a lot.” Jennifer Burns, sales director at David Wilson Homes NW, said the company hoped the donation would help the hospice continue its work across Rochdale. candidates.source_title: Rochdale and Bury record biggest driving test pass rate increases in Greater Manchester
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Rochdale and Bury recorded the largest increases in driving test pass rates across Greater Manchester in the year to March 2026, according to DVSA figures. Rochdale’s rate rose from 41.2 per cent to 48.3 per cent, while Bury’s increased from 40.3 per cent to 46.3 per cent. The changes represent increases of 7.1 percentage points at Rochdale and six percentage points at Bury compared with the previous financial year. Both centres remained below the Greater Manchester pass rate of 48.5 per cent and the Great Britain figure of 50 per cent. Across Greater Manchester’s nine centres, 52,716 of the 108,750 practical car tests taken between April 2025 and March 2026 resulted in a pass, according to the driving school’s analysis. Bredbury had the highest pass rate at 56 per cent. Bolton and Sale were the only other centres above the national figure, recording 51.8 per cent and 51.4 per cent respectively. Atherton had the lowest rate at 44.3 per cent, followed by Cheetham Hill at 44.7 per cent. Atif Iqbal, owner of Astra Driving School, said “Learners give themselves the best chance by practising on the kind of roads used around their test centre and taking a mock test before the real one.”

candidates.source_title: Rochdale residents return to homes after car smashes into building
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A suburban road has been re-opened after a car crashed into a house, causing a gas leak. Up to 55 householders were evacuated following the smash on Halifax Road in Rochdale shortly before 3am on Saturday (October 31, 2026). Today, a spokesman for Greater Manchester Police confirmed the road has been re-opened after the leak was 'contained'. Police were called to reports of a vehicle colliding with a property on Halifax Road at around 2.55am on Saturday. The collision went on to cause a confirmed gas leak, the force said. Click here to get the biggest stories straight to your inbox in our Daily Newsletter Up to 55 people were evacuated following the incident and a 50 metre cordon was put in place whilst investigations were ongoing. Two people were taken to hospital following the incident. Posting on social media on Saturday, Greater Manchester Police's Rochdale division said: "Emergency services are responding to an incident on Halifax Road, Rochdale, following a vehicle collision with a property at around 2:25am which has caused a confirmed gas leak. "Around 55 people have been evacuated and a 50-metre cordon is in place. The road remains closed while emergency services carry out their work." A spokesperson for Greater Manchester Fire and Rescue Service (GMFRS) said: “Shortly after 2.25am on Saturday 31 October, three fire engines from Rochdale and Littleborough fire stations attended a road traffic collision involving one car on Halifax Road, Rochdale. "Crews arrived quickly and used specialist equipment to make the area safe. Two casualties were taken to hospital by North West Ambulance Service. “Firefighters also assisted with the evacuation of nearby properties because of a gas leak caused by the collision. Overall, crews were in attendance for approximately four-and-a-half hours.”

candidates.source_title: Schools face financial challenges over pupil places - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: The financial and practical challenges surrounding the borough’s school places will be highlighted in each town next week. Rochdale Council’s township committees will hear that the lowest birth rate for 23 years is expected to present a “significant challenge” for the long-term financial sustainability of some primary schools within the borough — while 2027 is expected to see the highest number of students apply for the area’s secondary schools. A report to be presented to Heywood, Pennines, Middleton, Rochdale North and Rochdale South township committees reveals that the borough’s birth rate has seen a peak in Reception year pupils arriving in school in September, 2026, but, the birth rate for the intake in 2027 is 2,647 — the lowest since 2003. The report said: “A small number of schools have seen too many empty seats over the last few years as intake numbers reduced and a low intake in 2027 is going to see additional financial pressures on those schools. “Current birth rates indicate a steady but slow rise in the years to 2030. The current projected intake for 2030 is approximately 2,900 and includes children from new housing developments across the borough.” In September, 2024, 90 surplus Reception places were removed, followed by an additional 35 for September, 2025. The report warns that further reductions are needed in some areas of the borough where there are too many empty places. While recent years have seen an average of 113 children needing places after moving into the borough each year, this figure has fallen to 20 over the past two years. candidates.source_title: Port Vale find form in front of goal to sweep aside Rochdale - Alloa Advertiser
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Three early goals saw Port Vale ease to a 4-2 win at home to Rochdale in League Two. The Valiants had only hit six goals in 11 league games but with some dismal Dale defending they virtually sealed victory after 22 minutes. Onel Hernandez opened the scoring inside 90 seconds, gathering Kyle Dempsey’s through-ball and finding the bottom corner. Vale doubled their lead after 11 minutes. Aden Flint tripped Hernandez and George Byers fired the resulting penalty past Sam Waller. Dale threatened momentarily when Cian Hayes sent former Vale striker Dajaune Brown through, but he was thwarted by Jasper Moon. Moments later Vale scored their third. Dempsey’s shot was parried by Waller and Jordan Gabriel reacted first to slot home the rebound. With the game over as a contest, the second half produced few chances but ended with a flurry of goals. Dale’s Ian Henderson headed in after 82 minutes before Keyrol Figueroa restored Vale’s three-goal cushion with a simple tap-in four minutes from time.

candidates.source_title: £2.24m to bring derelict buildings back to life - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Empty and neglected buildings across the borough could be brought back into use with help from £2.24 million from the Government’s new Derelict Buildings Fund. Rochdale Council’s allocation, confirmed alongside Wednesday’s Budget, is part of a £125 million national fund to help councils transform derelict buildings into spaces their communities need. The money can be used to buy derelict buildings, close the viability gaps that stop regeneration schemes going ahead, and help community groups and local businesses take buildings over. Rochdale MP Paul Waugh will act as a Programme Champion for the fund. Government guidance will make clear that councils should work alongside local MPs when deciding which buildings and projects to back. The announcement comes as communities across the borough fight to save their locals. In Littleborough, there is strong interest in reopening The Wheatsheaf, part of the Grade II listed Roundhouse building dating from the early 1860s, which closed in June. Earlier this month, Rochdale Council passed a motion brought by Littleborough Lakeside Councillor Richard Jackson calling on the Government to block restrictive covenants on pub sales. Mr Waugh has supported this campaign directly having written to ministers urging action. These covenants allow pub companies selling a building to ban it from ever being used as a pub again, a restriction that binds every future owner. candidates.source_title: Albion prospect enjoying a new life and new role after big loan move to North West
candidates.source_body_excerpt: There are a few telltale signs which tell you Charlie Tasker has settled quickly and made a good early impression on loan a long way from home at Rochdale. Like the fact he has been a regular for the League Two outfit and has been entrusted with a new role on the left. Like the way the fans have taken to him and the club are happy for him to talk to a reporter from far-off Brighton even after a 5-0 home defeat. Or like the way he hasn't been back to Mile Oak yet and speaks about how he is enjoying not Manchester but "Manny". He isn't quite speaking like Danny Welbeck yet but the 20-year-old right-back is relishing his first EFL challenge after leaving Albion under-21s early in the season. Speaking after a session at Rochdale's training base near the site of Manchester City's old Maine Road home, he told The Argus: "This is my first loan, so I wanted to go somewhere where you think you have got a good chance of playing. "You know you are never guaranteed minutes in football. "But, when people were talking about Rochdale, when I spoke to the manager on the call, they play really attractive football. Similar to Brghton, actually.

Gymbound will become the club’s official club-wide main shirt sponsor, with its branding set to feature on the front of playing shirts across every section of the club, from its youngest players through to its senior teams as Rochdale Mayfield prepares to celebrate its historic 70th anniversary in 2028. The agreement will also see Gymbound, in Eagle Technology Park, Queensway, support Rochdale Mayfield’s open-age pre-season training programme, providing players with access to a modern fitness environment to help improve strength, conditioning, fitness and overall preparation ahead of the new season. The partnership will introduce exclusive membership opportunities for Rochdale Mayfield players and club members, encouraging greater participation in physical activity and making fitness more accessible. Rochdale Mayfield ARLFC founder Carl Abraham said: “We are absolutely delighted to welcome Gymbound on board as our club-wide main shirt sponsor for the 2027 and 2028 seasons. “This is a significant partnership for Rochdale Mayfield and another major step forward in our ambition to become the best amateur sports club in the borough. “As a club, we are constantly looking to build relationships with local businesses that share our values, ambitions and commitment to the community. Gymbound is a fantastic example of that. “What makes this partnership particularly exciting is that it goes far beyond simply having a company’s name on our playing shirts. The support Gymbound will provide through our open-age pre-season programme, alongside exclusive membership opportunities for our players and members, demonstrates a genuine commitment to investing in the health, fitness and wellbeing of our club.

candidates.source_title: Port Vale vs Rochdale: League Two stats & head-to-head - BBC
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Three early goals saw Port Vale ease to victory at home to Rochdale. The Valiants had only hit six goals in 11 league games but with some dismal Dale defending they virtually sealed victory after 22 minutes. Onel Hernandez opened the scoring inside 90 seconds, gathering Kyle Dempsey's through-ball and finding the bottom corner. Vale doubled their lead after 11 minutes. Aden Flint tripped Hernandez and George Byers fired the resulting penalty past Sam Waller. Dale threatened momentarily when Cian Hayes sent former Vale striker Dajaune Brown through, but he was thwarted by Jasper Moon. Moments later Vale scored their third. Dempsey's shot was parried by Waller and Jordan Gabriel reacted first to slot home the rebound. With the game over as a contest, the second half produced few chances but ended with a flurry of goals. Dale's Ian Henderson headed in after 82 minutes before Keyrol Figueroa restored Vale's three-goal cushion with a simple tap-in four minutes from time.

candidates.source_title: Affordable homes plan approved for town centre - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Plans for 27 new homes on vacant land in Rochdale town centre have been approved. Great Places Housing Group applied to Rochdale Council to create a development of 27 affordable dwellings, including a three-storey apartment building containing 23 apartments, and a 2.5-storey terrace of four family homes on the land at 206-208 Drake Street. The site, on the corner of Drake Street and Broadfield Stile and which backs on to the Grade II-registered Broadfield Park, is a former DVLA test centre which has been demolished and vacant for several years. Planning permission was previously granted on appeal to build 17 homes on the site but the scheme did not materialise. The site became overgrown and a target for fly-tippers before the council bought it via compulsory purchase to ensure redevelopment could go ahead. Supporting documents by Paddock Johnson architects state: “The scheme is proposed as 100% affordable housing for social rent, providing a mix of apartment accommodation and larger family homes within a sustainable urban location. “Its redevelopment for residential use would make effective use of an underused urban site in a sustainable location, with good access to local services, public transport, green infrastructure and town centre facilities. “The scheme provides 100% affordable housing for social rent, exceeding local policy requirements, responding to an identified housing need within Rochdale and providing a substantial public benefit. candidates.source_title: Inspector rules on garden fence rejected by council - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: A homeowner faces having to tear down a garden fence because of the impact it has on the neighbouring area. Rochdale Council refused Caterina Buonocore’s application for retrospective planning permission for the 1.55m high boundary fence — about twice the height of the original — around 19 Town House Road, Littleborough. She appealed that decision. But yesterday, a Planning Inspector rejected the appeal, stating: “The main issue is the effect of the appeal development on the character and appearance of the area. “Boundary treatments in the area are typically low-level and visually permeable, contributing to a sense of openness and allowing the soft landscaping within front gardens to remain appreciable. The existing greenery helps to soften the street scene and makes a positive contribution to the character and appearance of the area. “The appeal development introduces a close-boarded timber fence. The height, materials and extensive continuous form of enclosure contrasts with the more open and traditional forms of boundary treatment typically found in the locality. “On site, I observed that due to the prominent corner location, when seen from Park View against the back drop of traditional stone terraces with low-key forms of boundary treatment, the appeal development appears particularly stark and incongruous within the street scene. The Secretary of State will, by Order, establish a Mayoral development corporation for the Area. The name to be given to the Mayoral development corporation is the Middleton Co-operative Mayoral Development Corporation. Designating the town as a mayoral development corporation is expected to help speed up furthering economic development and regeneration in Middleton. The GMCA said: “The area presents a significant opportunity to improve Middleton town centre and its surrounding communities. “Establishing the Middleton Co-operative Mayoral Development Corporation will help attract public and private investment, bring forward new development and support the delivery of around 1,500 new homes, including affordable homes. candidates.source_title: Police target crime gang’s ‘spider web of criminality’ - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: Seventeen people have been arrested as police tackle a “spider web of criminality” in Heywood and Rochdale. This morning, 250 officers carried out a series of raids as part of Operation Rivercrest which is targeting an organised crime group. The operation led to the execution of 20 warrants – mostly in Rochdale and Heywood – as well as in areas across Bury, Salford, Manchester, Merseyside and Yorkshire. Those arrested range in age from 19 to 49. Sixteen men have been arrested on suspicion of various offences, including drugs supply, assault, violent disorder, affray, burglary, and robbery. One woman, aged 21, was arrested on suspicion of being concerned in the supply of drugs. DS Hannah Taala, of Greater Manchester Police’s Rochdale Division, said officers focused on the crime group after violence in Heywood earlier in the year . She said: “There was a large disorder in April, where multiple people were involved in violence in the Heywood area. “It ended in some quiet serious injuries, assaults, a stab wound, using vehicles in that disorder, weapons, machetes. A cannabis farm was discovered during the raids. Image: GMP

candidates.source_body_excerpt: Find out the latest events from October 31 from All Across the Arts columnist Steve Cooke A great opportunity to share ideas on how we can transform parks, public spaces and libraries into cultural and creative hubs for our communities. Building on conversations regarding ‘Third Spaces’ and ‘Everyday Utopias’ held with Kitty’s Launderette at a previous Lab Session, they are inviting partners and local residents to share ideas on how new strategies led by the council’s parks, libraries and culture teams might help enhance these spaces as free to access cultural and community spaces. The idea of a 'third space' comes from urban sociologist Ray Oldenburg, who described it as a social environment separate from home (the first space) and work (the second space). These are places where people gather, build community, share ideas and find a sense of belonging. The idea of “everyday utopias” is about enacting conventional activities in unusual ways. candidates.source_body_excerpt: A Greater Manchester Police officer who worked in Tameside has been dismissed after sharing confidential police information while in a relationship with a member of an organised crime group in Rochdale. Tubah Hamid was dismissed with immediate effect following an accelerated misconduct hearing held by GMP Chief Constable Sir Stephen Watson. The hearing found breaches of the standards of professional behaviour relating to Honesty and Integrity, Discreditable Conduct, Confidentiality, and Orders and Instructions were proven and amounted to gross misconduct. In his decision, Sir Stephen said Hamid's culpability was 'very high', describing her actions as 'deliberate, persistent' and carried out in the 'full knowledge' that they were 'unlawful and morally indefensible'. He said the former constable had abused her position of responsibility, with her misconduct involving multiple incidents over a lengthy period and deliberate breaches of policies governing information held on police systems. Sir Stephen added that Hamid's unlawful accessing of police data demonstrated a 'distinct lack of integrity and moral fibre' and said she was 'manifestly unsuited to the office of constable'. Hamid was dismissed with immediate effect, and her name was ordered to be added to the College of Policing's Barred List. The disciplinary proceedings followed a criminal investigation into Hamid's conduct.

candidates.source_title: Growing up, we could have benefited from better mental health support - Rochdale Times
candidates.source_body_excerpt: As a new trial offering better mental health and social care support is launched in Rochdale, Minister of State for Public Health and Patient Safety Dame Diana Johnson tells the Rochdale Times how it will help young people and their families across the borough. “How many of us could have benefited from the understanding and guidance of a mental health professional while we were growing up? Growing up can be challenging for any child. Professor Peter Fonagy’s recent independent review of mental health conditions, ADHD and autism has highlighted the scale of the challenge. Mental health distress is rising, particularly among children and young people, with girls especially affected. Greater Manchester is not immune to this disturbing trend. For children already facing difficult circumstances, the health risks can be even greater. Children in contact with social services often have high levels of mental health need, alongside other challenges affecting their lives and wellbeing. That’s why I’m delighted Greater Manchester will lead the way in improving early mental health support for children through Care Together, a pilot designed to give children involved with social care services faster access to help. Zulf Ahmed, Chief Executive Officer of KYP, said: “The Rochdale Diversity Awards are about recognising the people and organisations whose commitment, compassion and leadership make a real difference to others every day. “This year we received more than 130 nominations, each telling a story of someone breaking down barriers, creating opportunities or helping others to thrive. Bringing together more than 350 guests to celebrate those achievements was incredibly special. Rochdale MP Paul Waugh with some of the winners. Image: Paul Waugh “The awards remind us of the strength of our communities and the extraordinary things that happen when people come together with a shared commitment to making Rochdale a fairer, more inclusive and more connected borough.” The audience also heard inspiring contributions from civic and community leaders from across the borough.
